rationale: The target requires characterising the vehicle’s braking response where braking is required, not merely the surrounding collision risk. SG-1 and FR-7 establish braking behaviour itself as part of what must be evaluated, and H-1 connects omitted braking to failure to stop before collision. P stays at this vehicle-response level without incorporating supporting sensing, computation, communication, or control mechanisms or their timing constraints.
determining_elements: “The vehicle’s braking-relevant response” identifies behaviour directly required by SG-1 and FR-7, so including system response is justified.
“Where braking may be required to avoid collision” ties the response to the conditions relevant to evaluating omission of required braking.
The scope covers road users and static obstacles, including the pedestrian crossing 20 m ahead; these situations are supported by H-1 and FR-7.
The scope’s reference to evaluating whether braking is required specifies the operational context without adding an internal evaluation mechanism to P.
